courses.title: Direct editing 1 · Push and pull a face
courses.objective: Make a block taller by pulling its top face, then push the face back in.
courses.challenge: Pull the top face out 8 mm, then push it in 4 mm.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across and 12 mm deep.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: Direct editing changes faces of a part that already exists. A block with a hole has flat faces and a round one.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have your own part? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Click the top face
steps.learn: The top is the flat face on top. Pulling it out adds material, pushing it in removes material.
instructions: Click the face in the 3D view. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me and Aakar picks it.
steps.why: Direct editing always starts with the face you want to change.

checkpoint.expected: The face is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click it again. A face is a flat or round side of the part, not an edge.

guide.now: Click the top face of the block in the 3D view.

steps.title: Pull the top face out 8 mm
steps.learn: Offset face moves a face straight along its own direction. A positive number adds material. The sides stretch with it, so the block stays one clean part.
instructions: Open the Direct+ group and press Offset face.
Type 8 for the distance and press OK.
Or press Do it for me.
steps.why: This is push/pull: no sketch, no extrude, just the face.

checkpoint.expected: The block is 28 mm tall and the hole is still there.

steps.recovery: It did nothing? Check a face is orange first. Aakar says why in the status line if a move cannot be made.

guide.now: Press Offset face, type 8, press OK.

steps.title: Push the top face back in 4 mm
steps.learn: A negative number pushes the face into the part and removes material. If a move would hit another part of the solid, Aakar stops at the nearest distance that works and tells you.
instructions: Press Offset face again.
Type -4 and press OK.
steps.why: Push and pull are the same tool with the sign changed.

checkpoint.expected: The block is 24 mm tall.

steps.recovery: Still orange? The face stays selected, so just press Offset face again.

guide.now: Press Offset face, type -4, press OK.

steps.title: You can push and pull
steps.learn: Pick a face, press Offset face, type a distance. Plus adds, minus removes.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the tool did and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Pick a face, press Offset face, type a distance. Plus adds, minus removes.

courses.title: Direct editing 2 · Resize and move a hole
courses.objective: Make a hole bigger, then slide it across the block.
courses.challenge: Grow the hole by 3 mm, then move it 10 mm along X.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across and 12 mm deep.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: Direct editing changes faces of a part that already exists. A block with a hole has flat faces and a round one.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have your own part? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Click the wall of the hole
steps.learn: The hole has a round wall and a flat floor. Clicking the wall picks the whole round face.
instructions: Click the face in the 3D view. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me and Aakar picks it.
steps.why: Direct editing always starts with the face you want to change.

checkpoint.expected: The face is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click it again. A face is a flat or round side of the part, not an edge.

guide.now: Click the round wall of the hole in the 3D view.

steps.title: Make the hole 3 mm wider on each side
steps.learn: On a hole, a negative distance pushes the wall into the material, so the hole grows. Its centre stays where it is.
instructions: Press Offset face.
Type -3 and press OK.
steps.why: A round face changes its radius. Aakar keeps it a true cylinder.

checkpoint.expected: The hole is 22 mm across.

steps.recovery: The hole did not change? Pick the round wall, not the floor.

guide.now: Press Offset face, type -3, press OK.

steps.title: Move the hole 10 mm along X
steps.learn: Move hole / boss slides the whole hole. Aakar fills the old hole and cuts a new one in the new place, so the result is one clean solid.
instructions: Press Move hole / boss.
Type 10 for X, leave Y and Z at 0, press OK.
steps.why: A hole can move without redrawing any sketch.

checkpoint.expected: The hole sits 10 mm further along X.

steps.recovery: It says the move is not possible? The hole must stay inside the block; try a smaller distance.

guide.now: Press Move hole / boss, type X = 10, press OK.

steps.title: You can resize and move a hole
steps.learn: Offset face changes the radius. Move hole / boss slides it. Both keep the hole a true circle.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the tool did and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Offset face changes the radius. Move hole / boss slides it. Both keep the hole a true circle.

courses.title: Direct editing 3 · Delete a hole and heal the gap
courses.objective: Remove a hole by deleting its face. Aakar fills the gap.
courses.challenge: Delete the hole and check the top face is whole again.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across and 12 mm deep.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: Direct editing changes faces of a part that already exists. A block with a hole has flat faces and a round one.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have your own part? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Click the wall of the hole
steps.learn: Deleting a face removes it and heals the gap.
instructions: Click the face in the 3D view. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me and Aakar picks it.
steps.why: Direct editing always starts with the face you want to change.

checkpoint.expected: The face is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click it again. A face is a flat or round side of the part, not an edge.

guide.now: Click the round wall of the hole in the 3D view.

steps.title: Delete the face and heal
steps.learn: Delete face removes the wall. Aakar then fills the hole with matching material, so the top face becomes one whole face again.
instructions: Press Delete face in the ribbon (or right-click the face and choose Delete face).
Keep the mode on Heal and press OK.
steps.why: This undoes a feature without going back in the history.

checkpoint.expected: The hole is gone and the top is flat.

steps.recovery: A message says it cannot heal? Pick a face that belongs to a hole, boss, pocket, fillet or chamfer.

guide.now: Press Delete face, keep Heal, press OK.

steps.title: You can delete and heal
steps.learn: Delete face with Heal removes a hole, boss, pocket, fillet or chamfer and closes the gap.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the tool did and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Delete face with Heal removes a hole, boss, pocket, fillet or chamfer and closes the gap.

courses.title: Direct editing 4 · Tilt a face
courses.objective: Turn the flat top of the block into a gentle slope.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across and 12 mm deep.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: Direct editing changes faces of a part that already exists. A block with a hole has flat faces and a round one.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Click the top face
steps.learn: Tilt face turns a flat face about a line through its centre.
instructions: Click the face in the 3D view. It turns orange.
Or press Do it for me and Aakar picks it.
steps.why: Direct editing always starts with the face you want to change.

checkpoint.expected: The face is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click it again. A face is a flat or round side of the part, not an edge.

guide.now: Click the top face of the block in the 3D view.

steps.title: Tilt it 8 degrees
steps.learn: Material is added where the face rises and removed where it drops. The sides follow the new slope.
instructions: Press Tilt face in the Direct+ group.
Type 8 for the angle and press OK.
steps.why: A slope without any sketch or cut.

checkpoint.expected: The top slopes. One end is higher than the other.

steps.recovery: Nothing changed? A face with a hole can still tilt, but the tilt must not hit another face.

guide.now: Press Tilt face, type 8, press OK.

steps.title: You can tilt a face
steps.learn: Tilt face slopes a flat face by an angle. It refuses, with a reason, if the slope would hit other geometry.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the tool did and when to use it.

guide.cap: Done. Tilt face slopes a flat face by an angle. It refuses, with a reason, if the slope would hit other geometry.

courses.title: Direct editing 5 · Change a fillet radius
courses.objective: Round an edge, then change its radius without redoing the round.
courses.challenge: Round the top front edge with R3, then change it to R6.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across and 12 mm deep.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: Direct editing changes faces of a part that already exists. A block with a hole has flat faces and a round one.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have your own part? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Round the top front edge
steps.learn: Rounding makes a smooth fillet along an edge. Use the Round tool on one top edge of the block with a radius of 3 mm.
instructions: Click one top edge of the block.
Press Round and type 3.
steps.why: We need a fillet to change.

checkpoint.expected: One top edge is smoothly rounded.

steps.recovery: Not rounded? Pick an edge, not a face.

guide.now: Click a top edge, press Round, type 3, press OK.

steps.title: Click the rounded face
steps.learn: The fillet is a narrow curved face. Click it so it turns orange.
instructions: Click the curved strip along the rounded edge.
steps.why: Fillet radius works on the picked fillet face.

checkpoint.expected: The rounded strip is orange.

steps.recovery: Hard to hit? Zoom in, or press Select+ and choose Same radius.

guide.now: Click the rounded face.

steps.title: Make it R6
steps.learn: Fillet radius heals the old round away and rounds again with the new radius.
instructions: Press Fillet radius in the Direct+ group.
Type 6 and press OK.
steps.why: Changing a radius should be one number, not a rebuild.

checkpoint.expected: The rounded edge is clearly bigger.

steps.recovery: It refuses? Fillet radius works on 90 degree fillets between two flat faces.

guide.now: Press Fillet radius, type 6, press OK.

steps.title: You can change a fillet radius
steps.learn: Pick the rounded face, press Fillet radius, type a new number.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the tool did and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Pick the rounded face, press Fillet radius, type a new number.
